stories.headline: French stocks: ‘Buy when there’s blood in the streets’?
stories.claim: French stocks are deeply out of favour with investors amid political unrest, with the CAC 40 set for weak relative performance in 2026.
stories.summary: Investors are increasingly negative on French equities as riots and rising bond yields weigh on sentiment. A Bank of America fund manager survey shows a record number plan to underweight French stocks, and Barclays says French shares are now some investors' biggest short position. The CAC 40 is down about 5 per cent in 2026 and is on course for its biggest annual underperformance against European peers since 2010. Luxury names such as LVMH and Hermès, which weigh heavily on the index, have also struggled with weaker high-end demand. Some strategists argue cheap valuations and record earnings could tempt contrarians, though the 2027 presidential election and unresolved fiscal problems keep caution high.
key_points: Bank of America's monthly survey shows a record number of fund managers plan to underweight French stocks over the next year.
Barclays reports French shares are among some investors' largest short positions.
The CAC 40 is down about 5 per cent in 2026, lagging the broader European market for three straight years.
Luxury stocks such as LVMH and Hermès weigh heavily on the index and have struggled with weaker demand.
The index's price-earnings ratio has fallen from 16 to 13 even as analysts raised 2026 earnings growth forecasts to 24 per cent.
The 2027 presidential election and unresolved fiscal problems remain key risks for investors.
stories.market_take: Political risk and weak luxury demand keep pressure on French equities, though cheap valuations may attract contrarian buyers.

stories.headline: Japan insurers shift to longer bonds | NHK WORLD-JAPAN News
stories.claim: Japanese life insurers are shifting bond holdings into longer-dated government bonds as rates rise and bond prices fall.
stories.summary: Japanese life insurers are reallocating investments into longer-dated government bonds offering higher returns, as the Bank of Japan pushes interest rates higher. Falling bond prices have left the insurers with unrealised losses on their existing holdings. Meiji Yasuda Life plans to invest more than 2 trillion yen (about $12.7 billion) this fiscal year, mainly in 20 and 30-year bonds. Nippon Life made similar changes worth about $6.4 billion in the first half of the fiscal year, while Daiichi Life plans a similar reallocation over the full year, projected to lift annual earnings by about $216 million.

stories.headline: India's cartoonists built an audience online - now their posts are being restricted
stories.claim: Meta's Instagram has temporarily restricted cartoonist Satish Acharya's account in India, amid wider government content-restriction orders.
stories.summary: Indian cartoonist Satish Acharya says his Instagram account was blocked in India twice, first from 28 September to 6 October and again for three days earlier this week. Meta said it may temporarily restrict accounts to comply with India's IT Rules but did not explain the specific reasons. Another cartoonist, Manjul, saw a post criticising the election commission restricted. The Indian Express reported nearly 195,000 blocking orders were sent to platforms between March and July, though the data does not show how many posts were removed. The case raises concerns about political satire and free expression in India.

stories.headline: Funding set to double for plan to get rough sleepers off streets by Christmas
stories.claim: Government to double funding for plan to get every rough sleeper in England off the streets by Christmas, with £432m more in the Budget.
stories.summary: The government plans to add £432m to its rough sleeping initiative, raising total investment to £874m and extending support beyond March 2027 to the end of the Parliament. The pledge, made by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, aims to give every rough sleeper in England a route into accommodation by Christmas. The extra money is expected to be announced in Wednesday's Budget, ahead of a Rough Sleeping Summit at Downing Street. Critics, including the Conservatives, argue the policy has not worked, with England's rough sleeping at its highest level since records began in 2010. Homelessness groups want changes to Local Housing Allowance too.
key_points: An initial £442m package was announced, with a further £432m expected in Wednesday's Budget.
Total investment would reach £874m and extend support to the end of this Parliament.
The most recent official count found 4,793 people sleeping rough in England in autumn 2025.
More than 30 organisations have pledged support, and the National Housing Federation is identifying at least 2,000 homes and bed spaces.
The Conservatives criticised the record levels of rough sleeping, and homelessness groups urged wider reform such as restoring LHA rates.

The teardown examined the hinge, which it found more intricate than Apple's patents suggested, and identified possible causes for early inner-screen failures reported by owners. stories.headline: Israel’s election: The main issues in the words of the leading candidates
stories.claim: Israel's election on Tuesday centres on internal politics, with frontrunners largely agreeing on Gaza, the war with Iran and two-state policy.
stories.summary: Ahead of Tuesday's Israeli election, the leading candidates largely agree on the war in Gaza, the wars that followed, and the lack of a clear path to a two-state solution. The real divide is over Israel's internal politics and the future character of the state. Netanyahu's hard-right government faces a coalition of opponents promising a similar policy agenda but within the law. Key disputes include judicial overhaul, the attorney general's powers, Haredi conscription, and accountability for the October 2023 security failures.
key_points: The election is on Tuesday, and most leading contenders do not question the Gaza war or later conflicts, including the one with Iran.
Few contenders offer a clear route to a two-state solution, despite earlier Oslo commitments.
Main divisions concern judicial independence, including judicial appointments and a law curbing the attorney general's powers, both due to take effect after the vote.
Haredi conscription is a major issue, with Netanyahu reliant on Shas and United Torah Judaism for Knesset support.
Questions of political accountability for the 2023 security failures have dominated the campaign, though no inquiry into Netanyahu's own role has occurred.
stories.market_take: The outcome could affect Israeli assets and the shekel, though the article focuses on policy rather than markets.

stories.headline: Oxford Street: Stretch of famous London road becomes pedestrian-only
stories.claim: A large part of Oxford Street in London has become pedestrian-only as the first phase of a redesign begins.
stories.summary: Almost a kilometre of Oxford Street, between Orchard Street and Great Portland Street, was closed to all traffic including buses, taxis and bicycles on Monday morning. This is the first phase of a wider redesign led by the Oxford Street Development Corporation and Transport for London, described as a test and review stage. Several bus routes have been diverted and traffic is expected to increase on nearby streets. The full scheme is expected to be finished by spring 2027, with new trees and seats planned.

stories.headline: Donald Trump Attacks Bill Maher in Scathing, 1,318-Word Social Media Post: “Complete and Total Loser”
stories.claim: Trump attacks Bill Maher in a long Truth Social post after Maher's jokes about him and a White House dinner.
stories.summary: President Trump posted a 1,318-word attack on Truth Social calling comedian and HBO host Bill Maher a "complete and total loser". Trump targeted Maher's low ratings, disputed his claim that the second dinner lasted four hours, and attacked producer Chuck LaBella, who once worked on The Apprentice. The row followed jokes Maher made on Real Time about Trump's approval ratings and his comments about men's physiques. Trump also pushed back on Maher's remarks about a Vivek Ramaswamy campaign ad in Ohio.

stories.headline: Xi Jinping’s corruption crackdown in the spotlight as China prepares for meeting of top leaders
stories.claim: China's Communist Party opens its fifth plenum, focused on party discipline and anti-corruption, ahead of the 2027 congress.
stories.summary: China's Communist Party began its fifth plenum on Monday, a meeting of its Central Committee focused on party governance, discipline and anti-corruption. The Guardian reports that anti-graft investigations continue at pace, with more than one million people investigated last year, including over 100 officials at ministerial or provincial level. Analysts argue the campaign is also used to enforce loyalty and political unity under Xi Jinping. The meeting is seen as the last substantive gathering before next year's 21st Party Congress, where Xi is expected to secure a fourth term. Recent purges have reached the top military ranks, including the removal of Zhang Youxia and a sharp reduction in the Central Military Commission.
key_points: The fifth plenum of the Central Committee began on Monday and is focused on party self-governance.
More than one million people were investigated for corruption last year, including over 100 officials at ministerial or provincial level.
Analysts say the anti-graft campaign also targets political disloyalty and rivals.
Zhang Youxia, China's top general, was placed under investigation in January and later expelled from the party.
The Central Military Commission has been reduced to two members, Xi and Zhang Shengmin, and the plenum is likely the last before the 2027 congress.

Lula's victory marks his fourth, nonconsecutive term and reflects a campaign focused on continuity and social spending. He will govern a country that remains sharply divided.

The simulations suggest it forms through homogeneous nucleation, where vapour turns directly into ice without dust particles, a process not yet observed on any planet. stories.headline: There's a third PHP2Shell bug, but it won't get an emergency fix
stories.claim: A third PHP vulnerability, CVE-2026-115560, will be fixed in the next regular release rather than an emergency patch.
stories.summary: The PHP Foundation has reserved a CVE identifier for a third remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-115560, which it says is unlikely to be exploited in practice. It requires an uncommon combination of configuration and application code, and can be mitigated by disabling a session upload progress setting. The fix will come in the next regular PHP release, with only an informational advisory published for now. This follows the earlier PHP2Shell bugs, which were patched on Wednesday. As of Friday, no confirmed successful real-world attacks had been publicly attributed to PHP2Shell, though researchers report exploitation attempts and some proof-of-concept exploits circulating.
key_points: The PHP Foundation has reserved CVE-2026-115560 for a third remote code execution flaw in PHP.
The flaw needs a very specific configuration and application code, so the foundation does not expect it in practical use.
A mitigation is available by setting session.upload_progress.enabled to 0 until the next bugfix release.
The fix will be released with the next regular PHP update, not as an emergency patch.
The earlier PHP2Shell bugs, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, were disclosed and patched on Wednesday.

stories.headline: NASA updates lander plans for Moon landings, finally solves long-festering Orion issue
stories.claim: NASA lays out revised Artemis lander plans, including Orion docking in high-Earth orbit and a possible low-lunar orbit option.
stories.summary: At a news conference, NASA set out in detail how it plans to return astronauts to the Moon as soon as 2028, with revised architecture for the lunar landers. SpaceX's Starship will be refuelled in low-Earth orbit and dock with Orion in high-Earth orbit, while Blue Origin's plan involves four New Glenn launches without ship-to-ship refuelling. NASA is also working on an extended Centaur V upper stage with United Launch Alliance so Orion can reach low-lunar orbit. The number of Starship refuelling launches remains disputed, with a NASA safety panel citing about 22 and Elon Musk saying six to eight. Artemis III is still targeted for summer 2027.

stories.headline: Intel Tech Chief Says It Is Only A Few Percent Behind TSMC On Performance, But Catching Up In Scale Will Be Slow – VP Asserts High NA EUV Is The Right Choice
stories.claim: Intel executives say its process is only a few percent behind TSMC on performance and that catching up on scale will be slow.
stories.summary: Intel's manufacturing chief Chris Auth and CTO Pushkar Ranade spoke on the Dwarkesh podcast about Intel's position against TSMC. Auth argued that Intel's backside power delivery lets it print circuits directly with High NA EUV lithography, whereas TSMC needs double patterning. He said 14A is available in the process design kit and is being handled customer by customer. Ranade conceded TSMC is a much larger wafer maker but said Intel is already close on technology, perhaps a few percent behind on performance, power or density, and that execution and yield matter most.

stories.claim: Apple has closed seven French stores as protests continue, after two locations were looted a week earlier.
stories.summary: Seven Apple stores in France are closed on Saturday ahead of another round of demonstrations over living costs and school conditions. The closures include all three Paris stores and locations in Bordeaux, Lille, Strasbourg and Aix-en-Provence. Apple's Lille and Bordeaux stores were looted during the 17 October unrest, which saw peaceful mass protests turn violent in several cities. Reports say some stolen iPhones displayed warnings that they were disabled and being tracked. The closures appear to be a precaution, as stores with street-facing entrances are affected while mall stores are expected to operate normally.
